method: Evidence-bounded qualitative comparison; no numeric score

web.reason: The retained React production-Web run is broader and did not expose a required public UI-runtime origin. Flutter self-hosting and the required JS/Wasm blocklist run remain BLOCKED.

windowsNative.reason: Option A retains an installed full-flow result. Option B's native ABI is materially safer after Phase 3, but its hardened Dart-to-shim path and comparable Release build could not be executed here.

crossPlatformReuse.reason: The same Dart/Flutter UI source targets Web and Windows in the qualification slice. This advantage excludes the Windows-only C++ shim and self-hosted Web runtime assets.

maintenance.reason: Option A maintains React/TypeScript, WebView2, WPF and C# seams. Option B maintains Dart/Flutter plus a 495-line physical C++/header shim and CMake, and would also own renderer/font assets. Comparable staffing and long-run patch evidence are absent.

correctnessSecurity.reason: Option A has retained bridge/full-flow evidence; Option B now has stronger native ownership and cancellation evidence. Different-user/elevation, corporate deployment and the complete hardened Flutter path remain unresolved.

engineeringResult.reason: Mandatory Option B Flutter Windows, controlled-origin Web and Release-to-Release comparison evidence is unavailable. The native hardening result removes a correctness defect but does not complete the candidate comparison.
